title: A.R.M.O.R. state of the alarm of one node
description: What an ARMOR-NODE-ALARM node is doing: the phase and the mode of its panel, the siren, each zone and the last events. Published to armor/alarm/{node_id}/state (never retained). It carries a state, never a command (it may be signed, see sig): what the panel was asked to do travels in alarm_command.schema.json and what the node answered in alarm_result.schema.json.

siren.description: Whether the siren is sounding now.

locked_out.description: Whether the panel is refusing every PIN for a while after wrong ones.

commands_enabled.description: Whether the node accepts the commands of the server at all (its own setting; the broker's access list is a second, independent switch).

state.description: trouble: the node cannot read the zone (its converter or input does not answer); the zone is not guarding, it does not sound the siren and it stops an arming unless it is left out.

bypassed.description: Whether the zone is left out of this arming.

open_zones.description: The zones that would stop an arming right now.

events.description: The last events, oldest first, told as seconds ago because a node may have no clock.

arm_profiles.description: true when the node understands the arming profiles of the arm command. A node that does not say it (an older firmware) must be armed without a profile.

profile.description: The id of the arming profile the panel is armed (or arming) with; absent when it was armed without one or is not armed.

siren_loop.description: The state of the siren's wiring, present only on a node that supervises it (a return line read through the installer's resistors): ok the siren is there, open the wire is cut or the siren is gone, short the wire is shorted, unreadable the node cannot read the return line (the siren is not supervised), unknown until the first reading has held. Always sent together with siren_fault.

siren_fault.description: true when the siren's wiring is in fault (siren_loop is open, short or unreadable): the siren may not sound when the alarm needs it. Present only together with siren_loop.

seq.description: Present only in a signed state: a number that only goes up (the signer's time in milliseconds, raised by one when two states fall in the same millisecond). It comes together with sig.

sig.description: Present only in a signed state: the HMAC-SHA256 in hex, with the key of the installation, over armor-alarm-state|node_id|timestamp_ms|phase|mode|siren|locked_out|commands_enabled|open_zones|zones|seq (flags as 1 or 0, the lists joined by commas, a zone as id:state:bypassed). The fields it does not cover (events, profile, arm_profiles, siren_loop, siren_fault) are information and are not authenticated. A state without sig is valid and is not authenticated: a reader that needs to know who sent it refuses it.
